chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, and Sama'ah narrated, saying:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who was found breaking his fast three times during the month of Ramadan, and the case was referred to the Imam (peace be upon him) three times. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is killed on the third (time).'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for deliberately breaking the fast three times in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Samaanah reports that the Imam decrees execution (*qatl*) for one who deliberately breaks the fast on three separate occasions, highlighting the cumulative severity of the transgression. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view of deliberate fasting violation as a major sin warranting capital punishment upon repeated adjudication, distinguishing it from single-instance penalties. The reference to 'the Imam' underscores the authority of the Imam in applying this specific hadd punishment.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who was found breaking the Fast, three times during the Month of Ramazan, and it had been raised to the Imam<sup>asws</sup> three times. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> would kill him during the third (offense)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah, who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who destroys his fast in the month of Ramadan three times and is brought before the Imam three times. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is executed on the third time.’”
